{{Short description|Taiwanese physicist}}
'''Chii-Dong Lin''' (born 1946) is a Taiwanese physicist.

Lin was born in 1946, and is a native of [[Changhua County]].<ref>{{cite news |title=C. D. Lin's personal page |url=https://www.phys.ksu.edu/personal/cdlin/ |access-date=23 July 2023 |publisher=Kansas State University}}</ref> After graduating from [[National Taiwan University]] in 1969, he earned a doctorate from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1974 and was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Harvard University]] until 1976, when he joined the [[Kansas State University]] faculty.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="ksu">{{cite news |title=Chii-Dong Lin |url=https://www.phys.ksu.edu/about/people/faculty/lin.html |access-date=23 July 2023 |publisher=Kansas State University}}</ref><ref name="ksuscholar">{{cite news |title=Chii-Dong Lin University Distinguished Professor |url=https://scholars.proquest.com/gallery/ksu/profiles/9099C5B7CE47B01D01331CBDEDC1A4F1 |access-date=23 July 2023 |publisher=Kansas State University}}</ref> In 1985, Lin was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "[f]or his pioneering hyperspherical coordinate analyses of two electron atoms and ions, and his contribution to the development of the relativistic random phase approximation for atomic photoionization.<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=L&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=23 July 2023 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> In 1990, Lin was appointed to a distinguished professorship.<ref name="cv">{{cite news |title=Chii-Dong Lin (CV) |url=http://www.phys.nthu.edu.tw/~colloquium/vitae-2004-colloq-version.pdf |access-date=23 July 2023 |publisher=National Tsing Hua University |date=2004}}</ref>
